deck.h1: Everyone tokenises a promise. We tokenise a paper trail.
deck.p: A free grow journal underneath a real-world asset — documentation first, token second.
deck.p2: “Everyone tokenising real-world assets starts with the token. We started with the paperwork, because the paperwork is the asset.”

deck.div3: StatusPublic test network, test assets

deck.p3: Most real-world-asset products are strong at the token layer and weak exactly where it matters: the evidence that the physical thing exists and was handled the way somebody claims.
deck.p6: Holders get a number, not a story
deck.p7: Build the underneath first. The token is the easy part.
deck.p8: The journal is a product growers want on its own — free, no wallet, no crypto knowledge. That’s the acquisition channel and the data moat in one. The asset layer only turns on when a grower opts in.

deck.h25: Back it early. Own more of the harvest.
deck.p21: A grower opens a plant or batch for backing, adopters stake in, and earlier entry carries a heavier share weight because it carries more risk. Harvest proceeds split pro-rata.
deck.p22: Documents the grow · keeps the majority share
deck.p23: Backs early · weight by stage of entry
deck.p25: Weights are the designed model on devnet, not a live financial instrument. Nothing here is an offer or a return promise; see the risks page.
deck.p26: European cultivation rules are loosening, which means more people are being asked to document grows properly — and almost none of them have a decent way to do it. Meanwhile RWA capital keeps looking for assets that aren’t another fund wrapper.
